gaps.sentence: If the red light ___, the machine needs servicing.
gaps.hint: a general rule stated with if
gaps.explanation: Rules and general facts use the present simple in the if-clause: flashes.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ a muscle, apply ice at once.
gaps.hint: medical instruction, present simple after if
gaps.explanation: The if-clause of a conditional instruction uses the present simple, never 'will': pull.

gaps.sentence: If you order before midnight, delivery ___ nothing.
gaps.hint: result clause of a first conditional
gaps.explanation: The result of a real future condition takes 'will': will cost.

gaps.sentence: If the taxi ___ in five minutes, we are going to miss our flight.
gaps.hint: real future risk in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Real future conditions take the present simple in the if-clause: does not arrive.

gaps.sentence: Unless something urgent ___, I will be at my desk all morning.
gaps.hint: unless introduces the exception, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the exception to the plan and takes the present simple: comes up.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ his temper in the meeting yesterday.
gaps.hint: past regret with wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect: had not lost.

gaps.sentence: Unless you ___ the form by Friday, your application will not be considered.
gaps.hint: unless means if not, present simple
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not' and, like if, takes the present simple: submit.

gaps.sentence: If this medicine ___ relief within an hour, call me back.
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: does not bring.
